newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy to set minibudget after state account-source.
newsitem.headline: Italy to set minibudget after state account-source.

text.p: The Italian government will decide the size of its proposed mini-budget for 1997 only once quarterly state accounts have been presented, a source at the Italian Treasury said.

The source was responding to speculation in the financial markets about the date and size of extra budget deficit cutting measures the government wants to take to whip Italy into shape for European economic and monetary union (EMU).

The government has said the package will include structural measures. Newspapers have said it is expected to contain deficit cuts of 14-15 trillion lire to help the country meet the EMU goal of a budget deficit which is three percent of gross domestic product.
However the government has consistently said it will wait for official state accounts, due to be published shortly, before unveiling the mini-budget.
